page_title: Free Prompt Injection Checker — 31 Attack Patterns

sources.entry: LochBot - Free browser-based prompt injection vulnerability checker. Analyzes LLM system prompts against 31 attack patterns (jailbreaks, role override, data exfiltration) and returns a security score with remediation guidance. No signup, runs client-side.

summary.name: LochBot
summary.one_liner: A free, browser-based prompt injection checker that scores a chatbot's system prompt from 0 to 100 against 31 attack patterns and suggests fixes.
use_cases: Pre-deployment security review of a chatbot system prompt
Comparing security of different prompt designs
Documenting prompt security assessment for compliance
Training team members on prompt injection defenses
Getting specific fix suggestions for weak system prompts
summary.what_it_does: LochBot takes a pasted system prompt and checks it for defensive language and structure against 31 known prompt injection attack patterns across 7 categories: direct injection, context manipulation, delimiter attacks, data extraction, role play jailbreaks, encoding attacks, and prompt leaking. Each weakness is rated critical, high, medium, or low and rolled into a 0-100 score with a letter grade from A to F. For each failed test it gives a fix suggestion to add to the prompt. Results can be exported as JSON. The analysis is pattern matching and heuristics on the prompt text, not a test against a running model.
notable: Runs entirely client-side in JavaScript; the prompt is not sent to any server, according to the page
Returns a 0-100 score and letter grade with a fix suggestion per failed test
JSON export of the full vulnerability report
Source code is said to be available on GitHub
caveats: Structural pattern matching only; it does not send attacks to a deployed model, so red-team testing is still needed
Listed under a generic free label; no paid tier is mentioned on the page
